newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Telesp plans cellular expansion.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Telesp plans cellular expansion.

text.p: Telesp, a unit of the federal telecoms giant Telebras serving Sao Paulo, announced Tuesday it plans to invest 1.15 billion reais ($1.08 billion) to expand its cellular network by 1.5 million new lines by 1999.

Telesp President Carlos Eduardo Sampaio Doria told reporters the expansion will allow the firm to eliminate a two-year-old waiting list, meet exploding demand and prepare for competition with private cellular B Band frequency operators.
"This is good news for us here at Telesp and for the city and state of Sao Paulo," Sampaio Doria said during a news conference.
Telesp, the biggest of Telebras' 28 operating units, already is Latin America's largest cellular operator with 810,000 installed terminals just three years after it began offering such services.

Sampaio Doria said the company planned to install 480,000 analog lines by the end of 1998's first quarter, wiping out a waiting list of 323,073 prospective subscribers. Telesp also plans to reopen applications for new cellular lines after a hiatus of almost two-years.

Telesp also plans to install 460,000 digital terminals in 1998 and 560,000 in 1999. It was granted approval from its parent to seek bids for a private company to supply a digital system for Sao Paulo with a capacity of 1.2 million lines, he said.

Telebras SA President Fernando Xavier Ferreira, who also spoke during the news conference, said Telebras would conduct an "informal" survey of "legitimate cellular equipment suppliers" later this month and publish bid specifications in June.
He said the new digital system would require an investment of about 600 million reais, while the expansion of the analog system by 480,000 lines would cost 550 million reais.
Sampaio Doria said Telesp, as it begins accepting registrations for new lines, expects nominal demand to explode to between 4.0 million to 4.5 million new cellular terminals.

"This poses a giant problem but also a giant opportunity in terms of business and services," he said. "The Sao Paulo market is probably one of the surest investments in the world, comparable to the best markets in Europe."

Telesp's chief said real demand would likely reach about 3.5 million news lines, with a large slice of the pent-up demand to be taken up by the private B Band concessionaires, which are to begin operating next year in Sao Paulo city and state.

According to the Communications Ministry, there are some two million cellular subscribers in Brazil. The total is expected to grow to 15 million by 2000 as the country's telecommunications sector is privatized.
